HCM PlaybookHow to use it

Before you start

How to use this playbook.

01

Find the task

Guides are grouped into the eight HCM Academy topics. Use the contents page, or go to the topic's divider page for its list.

02

Follow the steps

Each guide is one page: when to use it, the steps in order, and the watch-outs that cause send-backs. The same steps are in the matching micro-learning course.

03

Check before you submit

Read the watch-outs before you click Submit. Bad data in is bad data out: what you enter flows into pay, costing, and reports.

Where things are. Oracle: Home page > Our Workforce > Quick Actions (Show More). Employee records: Our Workforce > Employment Info. UKG: Oracle Me tab > Apps > UKG (Kronos) Timesheets. Track approvals with the notifications bell.

This is a V.01 draft. Guides marked Pending SME review were built from Oracle documentation and official sources and are waiting on Vanderbilt review. The payroll calendar and your PCB consultant are the source of truth.

Online. Every guide links to its course at me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy. Questions: pcb@vanderbilt.edu

HCM Structure and Key Concepts

Overview6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are new to Oracle HCM, or a screen uses a term (legal employer, work relationship, assignment) you are not sure about.

  1. 1

    Start at the top: the enterprise and the legal employer.

  2. 2

    Know your business unit and department (work unit).

    • Department is often called a work unit at Vanderbilt and in reports.
  3. 3

    Tell a job from a position.

    • Vanderbilt jobs use six-digit job codes (job architecture).
  4. 4

    Understand the grade.

  5. 5

    Read the employment model: person, work relationship, assignment.

    • A person has only one primary work relationship and one primary assignment in it.
  6. 6

    Check the person type before you act.

Terms at a glance
TermWhat it means for you
Legal employerWho legally employs the person
Business unit / departmentWhere the person sits and is costed by default
Job vs. positionGeneric role vs. a specific seat in a department
Work relationshipThe employment link to a legal employer
AssignmentWhere job, pay, hours, and manager live

Watch-outs

  • Changes to a position can flow into every incumbent's assignment. Know which fields the position controls before you edit an assignment.
  • Do not reuse or repurpose a position for a different worker type; ask Compensation instead.
  • Open item: confirm which person types and work relationship types Vanderbilt uses and what each one means for pay.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/hcm-structure/ · Sources: Oracle: Overview of Workforce Structures; Oracle: Employment Model; Oracle: Overview of Loading Workers

HCM Workflow and Worklists

Oracle HCM5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou submitted a transaction and need to know where it is, or a task has landed on your worklist.

  1. 1

    Open the notifications bell at the top of Oracle.

  2. 2

    Find a transaction you submitted and check its status.

  3. 3

    Act on tasks assigned to you.

  4. 4

    Use Request More Information or send back instead of rejecting for small fixes.

  5. 5

    Withdraw your own transaction if you need to change it.

    • Withdraw is on by default in Oracle; your configuration may differ.
  6. 6

    Set up delegation before you are out.

Watch-outs

  • Check the bell daily, and before every payroll cutoff. A transaction waiting on an approver is not in payroll yet.
  • Rejecting means the whole approval chain starts over after resubmission; send back or request information when a small fix is all that is needed.
  • Open item: confirm Vanderbilt's approval chains by transaction type, whether delegation is enabled for HCMs, and the exact action labels on screen.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/workflow-worklists/ · Sources: Oracle: Approval Management Configuration Options for Oracle Fusion Human Capital Management; Oracle: How You Define Approvals for Human Capital Management; Oracle: Worklist and Email Notifications

Quick Actions and Viewing Person and Employment Information

Oracle HCM5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou need to look up a person or start any transaction for someone in your area.

  1. 1

    From the Oracle Home page, open Our Workforce.

  2. 2

    Click Show More to see every quick action.

  3. 3

    Open Employment Info and search for the person.

    • Use person number when names are similar.
  4. 4

    Read the assignment details.

  5. 5

    Review the history of changes.

  6. 6

    Check future-dated changes before you submit anything new.

Watch-outs

  • Do not start a transaction until you have confirmed the right person and the right assignment.
  • What you can see and do is controlled by your security role; a missing quick action usually means a role issue, not a system error.
  • Open item: confirm how HCMs view a record as of a past or future date on the Redwood Employment Info page at Vanderbilt.

FERPA Tutorial for Staff

Overview6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are working with a student worker's record or someone asks you for information about a student.

  1. 1

    Know what an education record is.

  2. 2

    Access requires a legitimate educational interest.

  3. 3

    Student worker records may be education records.

    • Treat student worker files with FERPA care.
  4. 4

    Directory information has limits.

  5. 5

    Get written consent for other disclosures.

  6. 6

    Do not pass information along.

Watch-outs

  • Do not confirm a student's class schedule, grades, or enrollment details to a caller, parent, or outside employer.
  • A student who opted out of directory information must not have even directory details released.
  • Open item: confirm Vanderbilt's FERPA office or Registrar contact, the required FERPA training, and how student worker records are classified.

I-9 and background check requirements by worker type

Process5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are bringing on a new person and need to know which checks must be complete before or soon after they start.

  1. 1

    Identify the worker type first.

  2. 2

    Look up the requirement in the table.

  3. 3

    Have the employee complete I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work.

  4. 4

    Complete I-9 Section 2 within three business days of the start date.

    • Example: start Monday, Section 2 due Thursday.
  5. 5

    Wait for clear to start when a background check applies.

  6. 6

    Request checks manually when there is no requisition.

Requirements by worker type
Worker typeI-9Background check
Student workersYesNo
Staff and facultyYesYes
Campus affiliatesNoYes
Service Free StipendNoNo
Student Expense OnlyNoNo

Watch-outs

  • Section 1 cannot wait for the three-day window; it is due on day one.
  • New York requires non-criminal background checks before any conditional offer.
  • Open item: confirm who completes Section 2 of the I-9 at Vanderbilt, in which system, and how remote hires are handled.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/i9-background-by-worker-type/ · Sources: USCIS: Completing Section 1, Employee Information and Attestation; USCIS: Completing Section 2, Employer Review and Attestation; USCIS: Handbook for Employers M-274, 2.0 Who Must Complete Form I-9

Employee or independent contractor?

Process6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenSomeone wants to pay a person for services through a contract or invoice instead of hiring them, especially a student.

  1. 1

    Ask who controls how the work is done.

  2. 2

    Ask who controls the business side.

  3. 3

    Look at the relationship.

  4. 4

    Apply the DOL economic reality test for wage and hour law.

    • Labels and pay method do not decide status.
  5. 5

    Treat students who perform services as employees.

  6. 6

    When in doubt, stop and ask before anyone starts.

Watch-outs

  • A request to pay a student by invoice, gift card, or stipend for work performed is a red flag; hire them as an employee.
  • Contractors are excluded from the new hire report; employees must be included.
  • Open item: confirm Vanderbilt's process and contact for worker classification questions.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/employee-vs-contractor/ · Sources: IRS: Topic no. 762, Independent contractor vs. employee; DOL: Fact Sheet 13, Employment Relationship Under the FLSA; IRS: Student exception to FICA tax

Data integrity: bad data in, bad data out

Overview5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are entering or changing any person, position, or assignment data and want to understand why each field matters.

  1. 1

    Follow the chain from position to pay.

  2. 2

    Know that positions push values to assignments.

  3. 3

    Check dates as carefully as values.

  4. 4

    Remember costing follows the data.

  5. 5

    Confirm what the position does not set.

  6. 6

    Review before you submit.

    • Check: person, effective date, position, hours, pay, costing.

Watch-outs

  • Fixes after payroll runs become retro adjustments in a later payroll and may mean a late or incorrect paycheck.
  • Never reactivate an inactive position or repurpose one across worker types to save time.
  • Open item: confirm which data errors Vanderbilt sees most often and who to contact for corrections.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/data-integrity/ · Sources: Oracle: How Position Synchronization Impacts Assignments; Oracle: Examples of Updating Date-Effective Objects; Oracle: Recalculate Payroll for Retroactive Changes

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Position Management

Job Architecture overview and how it impacts recruiting decisions

Overview4 min micro-learning

Use whenYou're creating a position or requisition and need to read a job code or title.

  1. 1

    Six-digit job codes are the job architecture.

  2. 2

    The job name carries its level.

  3. 3

    The job name becomes the business title.

  4. 4

    Compensation picks the job, not you.

  5. 5

    Skills come with the job.

  6. 6

    Pay ranges are tied to the job.

Watch-outs

  • A requisition whose job code doesn't match the pre-search memo is sent back.
  • Ask Compensation or your engagement consultant for the deck that shows the tracks and levels.

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Position Management

When to create a new position vs. update an existing position

Overview4 min micro-learning

Use whenYou're about to post or change a role and aren't sure whether to create or update a position.

  1. 1

    Create a new position for a new role.

  2. 2

    Create a new one instead of reactivating an inactive position.

  3. 3

    Create a new one instead of repurposing a vacant position for a different worker type.

  4. 4

    Create a new one when the business unit changes.

  5. 5

    Update the position when the same role changes.

  6. 6

    Fix the position before any requisition.

Watch-outs

  • Unsure? Ask your engagement consultant before you build anything.

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Position Management

Create a position

Oracle HCM8 min micro-learning

Use whenYou need a new position to recruit and hire into.

  1. 1

    Open Positions.

  2. 2

    Click Add (or Create).

  3. 3

    Effective date: today, not the start date.

  4. 4

    Status: Active. Action reason: New Position.

  5. 5

    Business unit, name, and code.

  6. 6

    Work unit: the department.

  7. 7

    Job: enter the six-digit job code from the pre-search memo.

  8. 8

    Location: where the person would sit on site.

  9. 9

    Assignment category: the one on the memo.

  10. 10

    Hours: keep Standard working hours at 40; set Working hours to the actual hours.

  11. 11

    Headcount and type.

  12. 12

    Overlap allowed: Yes. Then set Term or Flex if it applies.

    • Temporary: six months or less.
    • Term: a fixed role longer than six months, up to a year.
    • Flex: needed only part of the year, such as summer help who return each year. Usually non-exempt; set as temporary with 20 working hours so benefits don't kick in.
  13. 13

    Attach the pre-search memo and position description, add comments, and click Submit.

Fields that get positions sent back
FieldDo this
Standard working hoursAlways 40. Put actual hours in Working hours.
JobSix-digit code from the memo. No four- or five-digit codes (except VTS).
Assignment categoryNever Professional salaried non-exempt. VTS is always temporary.
ManagerLeave blank.
AttachmentsPre-search memo (required) and position description.

Watch-outs

  • Don't reactivate an inactive position. Old job codes on it can block updates and approval. Create a new one.
  • Don't repurpose an unused position that was built for a different worker type (for example, a student position for staff). Create a new one.
  • The requisition copies the position when it is submitted. Fix the position before you create the requisition.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/create-position/ · Sources: HCM training session 1, positions and pending workers, Sep 8, 2026

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Position Management

Update a position

Oracle HCM6 min micro-learning

Use whenA position's name, job code, or category changes, such as a reclassification.

  1. 1

    Open the position.

  2. 2

    Choose Update and enter the effective date.

  3. 3

    Pick the action reason that matches the change.

  4. 4

    Change the fields that changed.

  5. 5

    Attach the reclass memo, add comments, and click Submit.

  6. 6

    After approval, update the incumbent's assignment for what didn't flow.

Watch-outs

  • Position changes never reach an existing requisition. The requisition keeps the position as it was when submitted.
  • Reclassifications need Compensation's reclass memo before you update the position.

Position Management

Position management best practices

Overview4 min micro-learning

Use whenYou manage positions for your business unit and want to avoid send-backs.

  1. 1

    Create new; don't reactivate or repurpose.

  2. 2

    Use six-digit job codes only.

  3. 3

    Get the memo first.

  4. 4

    Standard working hours are always 40.

  5. 5

    Leave Manager blank on the position.

  6. 6

    Set the real location.

  7. 7

    Fix the position before the requisition.

  8. 8

    Keep documents on the position.

Watch-outs

  • When in doubt about a code, category, or location, ask your engagement consultant before you submit.

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Hiring

Create a requisition

Oracle Recruiting9 min micro-learning

Use whenAn approved position needs to be posted and recruited for.

  1. 1

    Check the position first.

  2. 2

    Open Hiring and click Create.

  3. 3

    Choose Standard and select the position.

  4. 4

    Requisition title: the posting title.

  5. 5

    Justification and openings.

    • Each opening is billed, and unfilled openings are billed at 50% to cancel.
    • More than one opening also goes to central finance for approval.
  6. 6

    Hiring manager and collaborators.

  7. 7

    Requisition type: Standard or Abbreviated.

    • Executive search is only for Cielo's executive search program. An outside firm (such as Korn Ferry) needs a PO requisition, not a recruiting requisition.
  8. 8

    Organization and primary location.

  9. 9

    Required details.

  10. 10

    Description: paste the position description.

  11. 11

    Offer info: workplace type.

  12. 12

    Attach the position description and pre-search memo.

  13. 13

    Configuration: candidate selection process and background check.

    • New York requires non-criminal checks before any conditional offer. The wrong process breaks that law.
  14. 14

    Click Save, then Submit.

Watch-outs

  • Never select Unlimited openings.
  • Never use United States as the location.
  • New York: New York candidate selection process and account VAN09, every time.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/create-requisition/ · Sources: HCM training session 2, requisitions and assignment changes, Sep 9, 2026

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Hiring

Convert a pending worker

Oracle HCM10 min micro-learning

Use whenYou got the clear to start email and the new hire is in your pending workers list.

  1. 1

    Open Pending Workers.

  2. 2

    Click the three dots next to the person, then Convert.

  3. 3

    Select the sections you'll update.

  4. 4

    When and why: action Hire, reason Employment.

    • Service free appointment: only for students receiving a stipend.
    • Non-employment: affiliates.
  5. 5

    Check the business unit and position.

  6. 6

    Biographical info: confirm date of birth and citizenship.

  7. 7

    National ID: Social Security number or a placeholder.

  8. 8

    Home address must be in the United States.

  9. 9

    Position overrides: review and continue.

  10. 10

    Assignment: person type, location, minors, expense account, status.

    • Location: override to where they'll actually work if remote (for example, Florida).
    • Working with minors: required; Yes triggers an additional check.
    • Default expense account: your department's usual account.
    • Assignment status: Active payroll eligible for anyone paid. Active no payroll only for affiliates; they won't appear in payroll even with a salary.
  11. 11

    Managers and work relationship.

  12. 12

    Payroll details.

  13. 13

    Salary: enter what they'll actually be paid.

  14. 14

    Review compensation, attach the offer letter, and click Submit.

Watch-outs

  • Never Quick Convert or Edit Pending Worker. Use Convert.
  • Active no payroll means no pay at all. Use it only for unpaid affiliates.
  • Not sure where a hire or transfer stands? Ask central recruiting before you create a direct hire.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/convert-pending-worker/ · Sources: HCM training session 1, positions and pending workers, Sep 8, 2026

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Hiring

Rehires and eligibility for rehire

Oracle Recruiting5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenA candidate you want to hire used to work at Vanderbilt, or you are terminating someone and need to set the rehire field.

  1. 1

    Know that the rehire field is set at termination.

    • Misconduct: No or Not specified, per your PCB consultant.
  2. 2

    Check the former employee's record before you commit.

  3. 3

    Let the recruiter review eligible for rehire.

  4. 4

    Never create a second person record.

  5. 5

    Convert the pending worker as you would any hire.

  6. 6

    Review costing on the new assignment.

Rehire recommendation at a glance
Value on terminationWhat it means for a rehire
YesEligible; recruiter proceeds through the normal process.
NoNot eligible without review; talk to the recruiter and your PCB consultant.
Not specifiedTreat as a flag; ask before moving forward.

Watch-outs

  • The rehire field is only as good as the termination entry. Set it carefully when you terminate someone; recruiters rely on it later.
  • Search inactive records before hiring a familiar name. A duplicate person record is hard to undo.
  • Open item: confirm with your engagement consultant (EC) who can approve rehiring someone marked No, and how Not specified is handled.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/rehire-eligibility/ · Sources: Oracle: Rehire a Worker; Oracle: Attributes for Worker Work Relationship

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Hiring

Staff

Process6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou need to hire a staff member and want to see every step from requisition to start date.

  1. 1

    Get the pre-search memo from Compensation.

  2. 2

    Create the position (or update one that fits).

  3. 3

    Create the requisition from the approved position.

  4. 4

    Work with the recruiter through interviews and the offer.

  5. 5

    Wait for background check clearance from PEBC.

  6. 6

    Convert the pending worker.

  7. 7

    Check costing on day one.

Watch-outs

  • Most hire problems start at the position. A wrong location, hours, or job code flows into the posting, the offer, and the first paycheck.
  • Don't convert until PEBC sends clear to start.
  • Open item: confirm with your engagement consultant (EC) any lead times between steps your area should plan for.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/hire-staff/ · Sources: Vanderbilt HCM training sessions; Oracle: How You Convert Pending Workers

HCM Playbook01 · Hiring

Hiring

Interns (Paid and Unpaid)

Overview6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenSomeone wants to bring on an intern, and you need to know whether the person must be paid and how to set them up.

  1. 1

    Start with one question: will the intern be paid?

  2. 2

    For an unpaid internship, apply the primary beneficiary test.

    • Clear understanding that there is no pay.
    • Training similar to an educational setting.
    • Tied to coursework or academic credit, and to the academic calendar.
  3. 3

    Check that the intern does not displace paid work.

  4. 4

    Limit the internship to its learning period.

  5. 5

    If the test is unclear, treat it as paid and ask.

  6. 6

    Set up the person with the right worker type and checks.

Paid vs. unpaid at a glance
ItemPaid internUnpaid intern
StatusEmployeeNot an employee only if the intern is the primary beneficiary
PayAt least minimum wage and overtimeNone; no expectation of pay
Setup in OracleHire for the worker typeOpen item: confirm category with your EC

Watch-outs

  • An unpaid intern who does regular work for the department may legally be an employee. Decide before the start date, not after.
  • Open item: confirm with your engagement consultant (EC) which Oracle worker type and category Vanderbilt uses for paid and unpaid interns, and which checks apply.
  • Open item: confirm with your EC whether any state where the intern works has stricter internship rules.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Payroll & Timecards

The HCM's role in payroll

Overview5 min micro-learning

Use whenYou are new to the HCM role, or you are not sure whether a pay issue is yours to fix.

  1. 1

    All new hires: you own the hire.

    • Process the hire correctly.
    • Confirm every payroll element is on the record.
  2. 2

    Exempt (monthly) employees: hands off, with two exceptions.

    • Add a compensation payment when needed, such as a lump sum.
    • Work an issue with payroll when one comes up.
  3. 3

    Weekly and biweekly employees: check time cards every week.

    • Confirm every time card is submitted.
    • Chase managers for missing or late time cards.
    • Escalate errors you can't resolve to payroll.
  4. 4

    Errors: you work them with payroll.

Watch-outs

  • Never try to run or rerun payroll yourself. That is payroll's job.
  • Open item: the exact payroll elements to confirm at hire are still being documented with the payroll team.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Payroll & Timecards

Review and approve time cards

UKG (Kronos)7 min micro-learning

Use whenYou are checking or approving non-exempt hours for a pay period.

  1. 1

    Open UKG from Oracle.

  2. 2

    Open the time cards for your employees.

    • Filter: in the row under the column headings, type your business unit under Business Unit (or your work unit under Work Unit), then select Refresh. Until you filter, the list shows everyone you have access to.
    • Each row shows the Approval State: Open, Submitted, or Approved (PayPrep Ready).
  3. 3

    Review each employee's status and hours.

  4. 4

    To check the open period, move to the current pay period.

  5. 5

    Act on a time card.

    • Approve: the hours are correct and ready for payroll.
    • Submit on their behalf: the employee couldn't submit.
    • Reject: send it back so it can be corrected.
  6. 6

    To enter hours for an employee, add a row on their time card and click Save.

    • In an open period, Save only. Don't submit.
  7. 7

    Confirm the result.

Watch-outs

  • Empty time cards early in an open period are normal.
  • In an open period, Save. Don't Submit. Submitting means you must edit, update, and resubmit later.
  • Once payroll signs off a time card, an approval can't be removed unless the sign-off is removed first.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Payroll & Timecards

UKG: Timecards, Time Off, and Schedules for Managers

UKG (Kronos)6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenA manager asks how to approve time, fix a missed punch, or respond to a time-off request, or a time card is not approved near the pay deadline.

  1. 1

    Open UKG from Oracle: Me tab > Apps > UKG (Kronos) Timesheets.

  2. 2

    Know the approval chain: employee approves, manager approves, payroll signs off.

    • Employee approves own time card
    • Manager approves
    • Payroll signs off
  3. 3

    Check the Approval State column for each employee.

  4. 4

    Resolve exceptions, such as missed punches, before approving.

  5. 5

    Review pending timecard changes the employee submitted.

  6. 6

    Approve or refuse time-off requests in Control Center.

  7. 7

    View schedules to confirm expected hours.

  8. 8

    Follow up weekly until every time card shows Approved.

Approval State column
StateWhat it means for you
OpenNot yet submitted or approved; follow up with employee and manager
SubmittedEmployee is done; manager approval is still needed
Approved (PayPrep Ready)Ready for payroll; no action needed

Watch-outs

  • Managers approve; payroll signs off. If a correction is needed after sign-off, contact payroll; the manager cannot simply remove approval.
  • Exempt employees' time off is managed in Oracle, not UKG. Only non-exempt time off is approved in UKG.
  • Open item: confirm the exact manager screens Vanderbilt uses (Manage Timecards, Control Center, schedule views), any delegate approver setup, and the manager approval deadline each pay period.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Compensation Management

Change salary

Oracle HCM8 min micro-learning

Use whenA salary changes outside the annual increase process.

  1. 1

    Open Change Salary for the employee.

    • Quick Actions > Change Salary > select the employee, or
    • Search the employee's name > Change Salary.
  2. 2

    Enter the effective date: when the new salary starts.

  3. 3

    Action: Change salary. Pick the reason.

  4. 4

    Click Continue.

  5. 5

    Enter the new salary.

    • A new amount (for example, $85,000), or
    • A percentage increase (for example, 2%).
  6. 6

    Review, then click Continue.

  7. 7

    File the supporting document on the personnel record.

  8. 8

    Add comments and attachments, then click Submit.

Reasons you'll use most
ReasonWhen
RetentionKeeping a flight risk. The most common outside annual increases.
ReclassRole reclassification. Also common.
MarketPay adjusted to market. Less common.
Counteroffer, EquityAs named.
Central HR updateCatch-all that needs documentation. Used for an FTE drop, such as 1.0 to 0.75 for an accommodation.
Exempt / non-exempt changeStatus change in either direction (FLSA exempt salary or FLSA non-exempt hourly).
Change in working hoursSalary only. Change the hours too: use Change Assignment with Salary selected.

Watch-outs

  • Annual increases and union requests have their own reasons. Don't use them for off-cycle changes.
  • Direct-hire reasons (no requisition) appear in the list. Ignore them here.
  • Oracle needs little in comments and attachments, but many departmental finance approvers want more. Confirm what your finance partner expects before you submit.
  • Exempt (monthly) payroll cutoff is around the 18th, usually the 15th to 18th, and earlier in December. The payroll calendar is the source of truth.

Course: me5231979.github.io/HCM_Academy/courses/change-salary/ · Sources: HCM SME walkthrough, Oct 20; Personnel Files: Document Records, Oracle User Guide

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Compensation Management

Process grossed-up additional compensation

Oracle HCM6 min micro-learning

Use whenThe employee should take home an exact amount of additional compensation.

  1. 1

    Open Individual Compensation for the employee.

    • Quick Actions > Individual Compensation > select the employee, or
    • Search the employee's name > Individual Compensation.
  2. 2

    Click Add, then choose One-time or recurring payment.

  3. 3

    Plan: Lump sum payment.

  4. 4

    Start date: the first day of the target payroll month.

  5. 5

    Enter the amount in the Net field (for example, $500).

  6. 6

    Leave Process separately set to Yes.

  7. 7

    Click Save.

  8. 8

    Submit, or click Continue to add comments or attachments first.

Watch-outs

  • Missed the cutoff (around the 18th)? Date it for next month.
  • Only change Process separately if payroll tells you to.
  • Pay goes to direct deposit, which is required.
  • Set the effective as-of date in Individual Compensation before you search for the employee. Otherwise you can't pick an earlier start date.
  • Attach the manager's request (email or memo) and say what the payment is for, so the approver doesn't send it back.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Compensation Management

Add a one-time payment (such as a sign-on bonus)

Oracle HCM6 min micro-learning

Use whenA taxable one-time payment needs to be added, such as a sign-on bonus left off the offer.

  1. 1

    Open Individual Compensation for the employee.

  2. 2

    Click Add, then choose One-time or recurring payment.

  3. 3

    Plan: pick the payment type, such as Bonus.

  4. 4

    Start date: the first day of the target payroll month (for example, Nov 1).

  5. 5

    Enter the amount in the Amount field, not Net (for example, $1,500).

  6. 6

    Leave Process separately set to Yes, then click Save.

  7. 7

    Click Continue, add comments or attachments, then Submit.

Watch-outs

  • Set the effective as-of date in Individual Compensation before you search for the employee. Otherwise you can't pick an earlier start date.
  • Adding the bonus to the offer is the preferred path. It processes in one transaction and reduces Oracle failures.
  • Amount = gross. Net = take-home. Mixing them up changes what the employee receives.

Compensation Management

Add a staff supplement

Oracle HCM7 min micro-learning

Use whenSomeone takes on extra duties for a period of time.

Which supplement (from the award compensation guide)
Plan (code)Use for
Administrative Supplement (ADS)Acting or interim in an administrative vacancy while a search runs. Expected less than a year.
Interim Appointment Supplement (INTERIM)Same situation, expected 12 months or more.
Temporary Supplement (TEMPSUP)Short-term additional responsibilities.
Not forFaculty, post-docs, students, or temps. Faculty have their own supplements.

Watch-outs

  • Ongoing supplements keep paying until someone ends them. Set a reminder.
  • Guide dated 01/17/2023. Confirm current plan names with finance.

HCM Playbook02 · Payroll

Compensation Management

Compensation impacts on payroll processing

Oracle HCM7 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are entering or reviewing a pay change and need to know which paycheck it will hit.

  1. 1

    The salary basis decides how pay is stored.

  2. 2

    Saving a salary change writes the person's element entry.

  3. 3

    The effective date says when the pay is earned; the cutoff says when it is paid.

    • Check the payroll calendar, not memory
  4. 4

    Backdated changes pay through retroactive processing.

  5. 5

    Some earnings are set to Process separately.

  6. 6

    Confirm the result before payday.

Which paycheck will it hit?
SituationTypical result
Approved before cutoff, effective this periodPaid this period
Approved after cutoff, effective this periodPaid next period with retro
Effective date in a past, paid periodRetro difference paid in a later run
Hourly rate change, non-exemptApplies to approved UKG hours in the period

Watch-outs

  • Pending approvals do not pay. A change still waiting in approvals at cutoff misses that payroll.
  • Retro only covers elements set up for retroactive pay. Do not promise a retro amount; payroll calculates it.
  • Open item: confirm with payroll which Vanderbilt earnings use Process separately and how retro shows on the payslip.

Add Assignment

Oracle HCM5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenAn employee already in Oracle is taking on a second job in addition to the one they have.

Leave Management

Entering and managing FMLA/TMLA transactions (continuous vs. intermittent)

Oracle Absence Management7 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou have an approved FMLA or TMLA leave and need to record it in Oracle.

  1. 1

    • Continuous: one start and end date
    • Intermittent or reduced: record time as it is taken
  2. 2

Continuous vs. intermittent vs. reduced schedule
TypeWhat it looks likeHow you enter it
ContinuousOne unbroken block of time offOne absence, start and end dates
IntermittentSeparate blocks for one reason (e.g., treatments)One absence per occurrence, actual time
Reduced scheduleFewer hours per day or weekActual hours missed, per day or week

Watch-outs

  • Intermittent leave entered as one long block overstates the time used. Enter only the time actually taken.

HCM Playbook05 · Costing

Costing Management

Costing fundamentals

Oracle HCM7 min micro-learning

Use whenYou need to decide whether an employee needs costing entered or can stay on the default.

  1. 1

    Know the three levels Vanderbilt uses.

    • Element (one type of pay on an assignment, such as a lump sum): if costed, that pay goes to the element's account.
    • Assignment (the person's job): if costed, all pay on the job follows it, except elements costed on their own.
    • Work unit default: every assignment sits in one work unit. With no specific costing, pay goes to the work unit's entity and financial unit, general unrestricted funds (05), the natural account for that type of pay, and program and activity 000.
  2. 2

    Open Costing for Persons.

  3. 3

    Search the person with Advanced Search and the right Effective As-of Date.

    • Use today's date (or the first day of the current pay period) to see what applies now.
  4. 4

    Select the person, then select the Assignment on the left.

  5. 5

    Read what you see.

  6. 6

    Ask your finance partner whether your department splits the work unit by program code.

    • No split: leave the default. Nothing to enter.
    • Split: enter costing for each person. Otherwise they default to program 000.
  7. 7

    Ask whether finance wants any role or payment tracked separately.

  8. 8

    Click Done.

Watch-outs

  • Some departments set default costing at the work unit level, others at the business unit level. Know which applies to you.
  • Costing touches payroll and financial reporting. Wrong costing charges the wrong budget.
  • Costing practice varies by department. Validate with your finance partner.

HCM Playbook05 · Costing

Costing Management

Enter costing for a person

Oracle HCM (Costing for Persons)10 min micro-learning

Use whenThe default won't work and the person or a payment needs specific costing.

  1. 1

    Open Costing for Persons.

  2. 2

    Search the person with Advanced Search and the right Effective As-of Date.

    • Use the first day of the current or future pay period the costing should start (the Pay Period Start Date on the payroll calendar).
    • Past date, such as a new hire's start: use that date. The standard path only offers today forward.
    • Prior pay periods (retro) also need the Retro Costing Request Form. See the watch-outs.
  3. 3

    Select the person, then select the Assignment on the left.

  4. 4

    Click Actions > Create and choose what to cost.

    • Create Costing: the whole assignment.
    • Create Costing of Element: one type of pay, such as a bonus. Then pick the Element Name; use the code ending in Earnings Results (for example, BON Earnings Results). Codes are listed in the HCM Award Compensation Resource Guide on the HCM Specialist resource page.
  5. 5

    Enter the effective date and click OK.

  6. 6

    Add a costing line: click Actions > Create, or the + icon.

  7. 7

    Enter each line. Percentages must total 100%.

    • COA string: Entity, Net Asset Class (for example, 05), Financial Unit, Program and Activity (000 if unused), VU_Function. Use default zeros for InterEntity (000), Future 2 (0), and the POET fields (0000).
    • Account: leave it blank for an assignment (payroll fills it). For an element, enter it: 5110 faculty, 5120 staff, 5130 student.
    • POET string (grants): in the COA fields always enter the payroll clearing string 380.05.38600.5140.000.000.000.VUI.0, then Project Number, Organization, Expenditure Type (SalFac, SalStaff, or SalStud), and Task.
    • Leave Allocation Type blank.
  8. 8

    Click Submit.

  9. 9

    Click Done, then run the HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan report.

Watch-outs

  • Costing applies to a full pay period. Oracle uses the costing in effect on the Pay Period End Date and does not prorate.
  • Current and future changes: enter by the HCM Transaction Cutoff.
  • Prior periods (retro): also submit the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary) to the Research Finance Team by the Retro Change Cutoff, usually two business days before the HCM Transaction Cutoff. Include a cost transfer memo if an externally funded grant is affected.
  • Vanderbilt's guide is dated 01/27/2022, before the Redwood screens. Confirm field names in a recorded demo.

HCM Playbook05 · Costing

Costing Management

Change existing costing

Oracle HCM (Costing for Persons)10 min micro-learning

Use whenCosting already exists and needs to start differently, be fixed, stop, or be removed.

  1. 1

    Decide which action you need.

  2. 2

    Open Costing for Persons and search with the action's date.

    • Update, Correct, or Delete Record: the first day of the pay period the change applies to.
    • End Date: the last day of the pay period the costing should apply to.
  3. 3

    Select the Assignment (or Element) on the left.

  4. 4

    Click History and review every costing period.

  5. 5

    Click Edit and choose the action.

    • Update: enter the new costing lines. With no end date, it continues going forward.
    • Correct: enter the costing as it should have been for the whole selected period.
    • End Date: stops all costing from that date. An assignment returns to the work unit default; an element returns to the assignment's costing.
    • Delete Record: confirm the pop-up with OK. The previous record's end date extends to close the gap.
  6. 6

    Enter or adjust the lines so they total 100%, then click Submit.

  7. 7

    Prior periods: submit the Retro Costing Request Form (Salary).

  8. 8

    Click Done, then run the HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan report.

Which action, which search date
ActionUse it toSearch on
UpdateStart a different costing as of a date. History is kept and a new record is added.First day of the pay period the new costing starts
CorrectRevise an existing costing for its entire date range.First day of the pay period it should have started
End DateStop costing as of a pay period end date.Last day of the last pay period it should apply
Delete RecordRemove a costing record completely.First day of the pay period of the record to remove

Watch-outs

  • Don't End Date a prior period if you want to keep costing records that come after that date. End Date ends everything from that date forward.
  • After End Date, use Create (not Update) to add costing again later.
  • Dates matter most. Check History before every change.
  • Vanderbilt's guide is dated 01/27/2022, before the Redwood screens. Confirm labels in a recorded demo.

    Decide the setup: paid student worker, service free stipend, or student expense only.

    • Paid work: Student Workers course
    • Stipend, no services: Service Free Stipend course
    • Reimbursement only: Student Expense Only course
  2. 2

    Check the person's existing record before you add anything.

  3. 3

    Add a Work Relationship for an N-only record; add an assignment if an E assignment exists.

  4. 4

    Complete the compliance step that matches the setup.

    • I-9 Section 2 due within 3 business days of first paid day
  5. 5

    Use the right hire reason and status when you convert or hire.

  6. 6

    Track approvals and confirm the record before payroll cutoff.

Requirements by student setup
SetupI-9Background check
Student worker (paid)YesNo
Service Free StipendNoNo
Student Expense OnlyNoNo

Watch-outs

  • Do not use a stipend or expense-only setup to pay a student for work. If the student performs services for pay, they are a student worker.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt owner for student eligibility (enrollment, hour limits, international student work authorization) is not yet documented. Confirm with your PCB consultant.
  • Open item: Whether student hires come through Oracle Recruiting requisitions or a direct hire in your area.

HCM Playbook06 · Students & Faculty

Students

Student Workers

Oracle HCM6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenA department wants to pay an enrolled student for work and you need to set up or extend the record.

  1. 1

    Search the student in Our Workforce > Employment Info.

  2. 2

    N record only: add the employment Work Relationship. Existing E assignment: add an assignment.

    • N only: add Work Relationship
    • Has E: Add Assignment
  3. 3

    Enter the position and assignment details, including the end date.

  4. 4

    Set hire reason Hire employment and status Active payroll eligible.

  5. 5

    Complete the I-9 within three business days of the first paid day. No background check.

    • Original documents, examined in person
  6. 6

    Submit, track approval with the notifications bell, then confirm costing and UKG.

Watch-outs

  • An end date that does not match the work period keeps a student active and payable after they stop working. Review end dates at every term change.
  • Graduate teaching and research assistants may be treated differently under the FLSA (DOL Fact Sheet #17S). Do not decide exemption yourself; ask Compensation.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt rules on student hour limits, eligibility checks, and who confirms enrollment are not yet documented.

Students

Add a Work Relationship or add an Assignment?

Oracle HCM4 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou are about to set up paid work for a student and need to pick Add Work Relationship or Add Assignment.

Pick the action
Student hasAction
Only an enrolled student (N) recordAdd the employment Work Relationship

HCM Playbook06 · Students & Faculty

Changes and Approvals

Student and faculty assignment changes

Oracle HCM6 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenA term is ending or starting and a student or faculty assignment needs to change or end.

  1. 1

    Start at Our Workforce > Employment Info and search the person.

  2. 2

    Use a direct action for a single change.

    • One field: direct action
    • Several fields: Change Assignment
  3. 3

    To end an assignment at term end, use End Assignment in Change Assignment.

  4. 4

    Use a transfer, not Change Assignment, to move someone to another position in the BU.

  5. 5

    Review costing and fields that do not flow from the position.

  6. 6

    Submit before payroll cutoff and track approval with the notifications bell.

Watch-outs

  • An assignment left open past term end keeps a student or faculty member active and payable.
  • Moving a person to another position in the BU is a transfer. Do not use Change Assignment for it.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt's term-change calendar and whether student assignments are ended or extended in bulk.

HCM Playbook74
HCM Playbook07 · Records

Document Records & Reporting

Add a document record

Oracle HCM (Document Records)7 min micro-learning

Use whenYou have a final, signed document to file: discipline, a compensation letter, a performance review, or a leave or accommodation approval.

  1. 1

    Open Document Records for the employee.

  2. 2

    Click Add.

  3. 3

    Document Type: pick the type that matches.

  4. 4

    Name: use the naming convention shown in the description.

  5. 5

    Issued On: the date the document was presented to the employee.

  6. 6

    From Date and To Date: the period the document covers.

  7. 7

    Leave Issuing Comments and Context Value blank.

  8. 8

    Attach the final signed copy and click Submit.

Types, names, and dates
Document TypeUse for, names, and dates
Performance and DisciplineWritten, Final, or Termination level (Discipline or PACP). Names like "Written Warning - Discipline". Discipline: To Date is 12 months after the From Date. PACP: To Date is the end of the plan (for example, 90 days).
Compensation LettersAnnual increase, bonus, interim pay, and salary increase letters (equity, market, reclass). Use From and To Date for interim or time-limited pay.
Performance ReviewAny review or goal-setting document. Names like "Performance Review - (review dates)". From and To Date = the period reviewed.
Leave and Accommodation DocumentationApproval letters for FMLA, Non-FMLA, State Leave, Personal Leave, and Accommodation. From and To Date = the approved timeframe.

Watch-outs

  • Attach only the final signed copy.
  • Questions about which type to use go to your HR Consultant.
  • Confirm the exact Document Records menu path in Vanderbilt's Oracle during a recorded demo.

Introduction to BI Reporting and the Departmental Playbook

Oracle BI (OTBI)5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou need a list or check across your area, such as everyone's costing, rather than one person's record.

  1. 1

    Open Reports and Analytics (Navigator > Tools > Reports and Analytics).

  2. 2

    Know the folders: Shared Folders for official reports, My Folders for yours.

  3. 3

    Search or browse to the report, then click its name to open it.

  4. 4

    • HCM Assignment Cost Allocation Plan
    • HCM Element Cost Allocation Plan
    • HCM Cost Allocation Verification Plan
  5. 5

Watch-outs

  • Bad data in, bad data out. A report only reflects what was entered in Oracle.
  • Do not save changes over a shared report. Save your own copy in My Folders.
  • Open item: confirm where the Departmental Playbook lives in the catalog (folder path) and whether Vanderbilt exposes Reports and Analytics on a different menu.

Reporting 101

Oracle BI (OTBI)5 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenYou need to run an existing catalog report for your area and trust what it shows.

  1. 1

    Open Reports and Analytics and find the report.

  2. 2

    Answer the prompts.

  3. 3

    Set the as-of or effective date.

  4. 4

    Run the report and wait for results.

  5. 5

    Read the results with the prompts in mind.

  6. 6

Watch-outs

  • Date matters. A person hired next week will not appear on a report run as of today.

Pick the right output
NeedUse
Shareable, formatted viewExport Formatted (Excel or PDF)
Data to sort or pivotExport Data (CSV or Excel)
Same report every weekSchedule an agent

HCM Playbook07 · Records

Document Records & Reporting

Reporting 301

Oracle BI (OTBI)8 min micro-learningPending SME review

Use whenNo catalog or Playbook report gives you the columns or filters you need.

  1. 1

    Create a new analysis and pick a subject area.

  2. 2

    Add only the columns you need on the Criteria tab.

  3. 3

    Add filters to limit rows.

  4. 4

    Add prompts if others will run it for different values.

  5. 5

    Check results against known records.

  6. 6

    Save to My Folders.

Watch-outs

  • Hiding a column is not security. Data security comes from Oracle roles, and every viewer sees only what their roles allow.
  • If you do not see Create > Analysis, you may not have a BI author role.
  • Open item: confirm which BI roles HCMs have, who can publish to Shared Folders > Custom, and the request process for new shared reports.
